title: Billing Rule on One Delivery Charge per Address per Day (Ridgeline Orders & Delivery)
content:
**Billing rule.** Ridgeline Orders & Delivery orders of one customer delivered by Ridgeline trucks to the same address on the same day are charged one delivery charge. When the customer already has one or more orders with a delivery charge billed for that delivery date and that address, no further delivery charge is billed for that date and address, and the charge kept is the highest program delivery charge among those orders. Haul-away and basic install charges are billed per order regardless of consolidation, and shipped orders are never consolidated.

## Terms used in the rule

- **Orders already charged for the date and address.** The count, across the customer's orders to that same delivery address, of orders that already have a delivery charge billed for that delivery date.
- **Program delivery charge.** The per-order delivery charge of the fulfillment program each order is placed under.
- **Shipped orders.** Orders sent by the carrier; they never join a consolidation.

## Condition and result

| Delivered by Ridgeline trucks, same customer, same address, same day | Orders already charged for that date and address | Result for this rule |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | None | The rule has not yet been triggered for that date and address |
| Yes | One or more | No further delivery charge is billed for that date and address; the one charge kept is the highest program delivery charge among those orders |
| The order is shipped | Any | Never consolidated |

Haul-away and basic install charges sit outside this table: each order that books them is billed them, whether or not its delivery charge is consolidated.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A customer has two orders delivered by Ridgeline trucks to one address on the same day. Order A, under a program whose delivery charge is assumed to be $40.00, has its delivery charge billed first. Order B is under a program whose delivery charge is assumed to be $70.00 and has haul-away booked at an assumed $30.00.

1. When Order B is billed, one order already has a delivery charge billed for that date and address, so no further delivery charge is billed for Order B.
2. The one delivery charge kept for that date and address is the higher of $40.00 and $70.00, namely $70.00.
3. Order B is still billed its haul-away charge of $30.00, because haul-away is billed per order.

Had Order B been delivered to a different address, or on a different day, the two orders would not share a date and address and this rule would not join them. A shipped order to the same address on that day would never be consolidated with them.
